title: AF-1-part-2
description: Airframe exam covering aircraft rigging, leveling, control surface travel and balancing, cable systems, hardware practices, and manufacturing/assembly procedures, drawn from the AF-1 rigging question/answer bank.

questions.question: When should rigging of an aircraft be performed?
options: A. Whenever there is a problem with alignment
B. Only at the first annual inspection
C. Only when the aircraft is painted
questions.explanation: Rigging is carried out whenever misalignment of flight controls or structure is suspected or detected, not on a fixed arbitrary schedule.

questions.question: Which part increases wing camber, increases lift, and helps control the aircraft at low speed?
questions.explanation: Flaps increase camber and wing area, producing more lift and allowing safe, controllable flight at lower airspeeds such as takeoff and landing.

questions.question: What is used to counteract the effects of engine and propeller torque?
options: B. Wash-in and wash-out (differential wing twist)
questions.explanation: Differential wing twist (wash-in on one wing, wash-out on the other) is used to offset the asymmetric lift caused by engine/propeller torque effects.

questions.question: What must be done before checking the position or angle of a main component of an aircraft?
options: B. Jacking and leveling the aircraft
questions.explanation: The aircraft must first be jacked and leveled so that all rigging measurements are taken from a known, consistent reference attitude.

questions.question: Which balancing method does not require removal of the control surface?
questions.explanation: The calculation method determines balance using measured weights and distances without physically removing the control surface from the aircraft.

questions.question: A wooden cradle used in aircraft structural work is best described as what?
options: A. Supports cut to conform to the shape of the fuselage frame
C. A type of control lock
questions.explanation: A wooden cradle is custom-cut so its supports match the contour of the fuselage frame, cradling the structure securely during work.

questions.question: Where an angular or twisting motion is needed in a control system, what is typically installed?
questions.explanation: A torque tube transmits rotary (twisting) motion through a control system where a straight push-pull or cable run cannot do so.

questions.question: If the top of a landing gear wheel leans inboard relative to the vertical, what is this called?
questions.explanation: When the top of the wheel tilts inward (toward the aircraft centerline), this out-of-vertical condition is called negative camber.

questions.question: What are the two very important alignments that must be checked for an airplane's wings?
options: A. Sweep angle and aspect ratio
B. Angle of incidence and dihedral
questions.explanation: Wing rigging checks focus on angle of incidence (relative to the fuselage) and dihedral (the upward wing angle), both critical to flight characteristics.

questions.question: Which balancing method uses a scale graduated in hundreds of pounds?
options: B. Reaction method using a known weight only
C. Scale method of a pound
questions.explanation: This balancing method directly reads the reaction force on a scale graduated in hundreds of pounds to determine control surface balance.

questions.question: If no specific direction is given for inserting a bolt, which way should it be installed?
options: A. With the bolt head down or aft
B. In whichever direction is most convenient
C. With the bolt head up or forward
questions.explanation: The standard practice, absent other instructions, is to install bolts with the head up or forward so that, if the nut loosens, gravity/airflow works against it falling out.

questions.question: A twist in an airplane wing that decreases its angle of incidence near the tip is called what?
questions.explanation: Wash-out reduces the angle of incidence toward the wingtip, which helps the wing root stall before the tip, preserving aileron control.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT used to measure control surface travel?
questions.explanation: A spirit level is used for leveling the aircraft, not for measuring the angular travel of a control surface.

questions.question: A 7x7 construction cable is generally classified as what type of cable?
questions.explanation: 7x7 (7 strands of 7 wires) cable is a medium-flexibility cable, more flexible than 1x19 but less flexible than 7x19 cable.

questions.question: What instrument is used for measuring the angle of incidence of a wing?
questions.explanation: An incidence board is placed on the wing at specified rib stations to measure the angle of incidence against a reference.

questions.question: What effect does lengthening the rear wing strut have?
options: A. Decreases the angle of incidence and washes the wing out
B. Increases the angle of incidence and washes the wing in
C. Has no effect on incidence or wash
questions.explanation: Lengthening the rear strut rotates the trailing edge of the wing down relative to the front attachment, decreasing incidence and introducing wash-out.

questions.question: Control surface travel stops are checked relative to what?
options: B. Prior to flight, against the manufacturer's specified travel limits
C. Only during annual inspection of the engine
questions.explanation: Control surface travel (stop) limits are checked against the specified maximum and minimum deflections before flight operations.

questions.question: A castle nut is designed to be secured by what?
questions.explanation: The slots in a castellated (castle) nut are designed to align with a hole in the bolt so a cotter pin can be inserted to prevent the nut from turning.

questions.question: What tools are used to measure the dihedral angle of a wing?
options: A. A tensiometer and a protractor
B. A straightedge and an inclinometer
C. A plumb bob and a turnbuckle
questions.explanation: Dihedral is measured by placing a straightedge across wing reference points and reading the angle with an inclinometer.

questions.question: What is the first step to correct the amount of travel of a flap?
options: C. Check the motor and drive assembly
questions.explanation: Incorrect flap travel is first traced to the flap motor and drive mechanism before adjusting limit switches or linkages.

questions.question: Which of the following describes proper hardware assembly procedure?
options: A. Always use the longest bolt available
B. Always add extra washers for safety
C. Don't use a stack of washers to make up for a bolt with too long a grip length
questions.explanation: Using a bolt that is too long and stacking washers to compensate is poor practice; the correct grip-length bolt should be selected instead.

questions.question: Incorrect rigging of the rudder primarily affects which aircraft motion?
questions.explanation: The rudder controls yaw about the vertical axis, so rudder rigging errors most directly affect yaw control and response.

questions.question: Which tool is used to check structural/wing symmetry on an aircraft?
questions.explanation: A surveyor's transit (or similar sighting instrument) is used to check that the wings and tail are symmetrically positioned about the aircraft's centerline.

questions.question: What do some aircraft use for longitudinal and lateral leveling?
options: B. A protractor and torque wrench
C. A plumb bob and grid plate
questions.explanation: A plumb bob suspended over a marked grid plate lets technicians check that the aircraft is level both longitudinally and laterally.

questions.question: On cantilever aircraft, what is adjusted on the rear spar to change the dihedral angle?
questions.explanation: An eccentric bushing at the rear spar attachment can be rotated to fine-tune the wing's dihedral angle on cantilever wing designs.

questions.question: What is the component, made from non-metal or soft metal, through which a control cable passes at a bulkhead?
questions.explanation: A fairlead guides a cable through a structural opening (such as a bulkhead) and is made of a soft material to avoid abrading the cable.

questions.question: What must be considered when using jacks to raise an aircraft?
options: B. The jack point locations and load limits
C. Only the hydraulic fluid color
questions.explanation: Jacking must use the manufacturer's designated jack points and must not exceed the specified load limit for the jack and structure.

questions.question: Which part of a cable tensiometer connects to the indicator?
questions.explanation: The riser is the part of the tensiometer that contacts the cable and transmits the deflection force to the indicator mechanism.

questions.question: A change in direction of a control cable run is typically accomplished by what?
questions.explanation: Pulleys are used to change the direction of a cable run while allowing the cable to move freely with minimal friction.

questions.question: In which manual would you find the specified control surface travel movements?
options: B. The pilot's operating handbook only
C. The weight and balance manual
questions.explanation: Control surface travel limits and rigging data are specified in the aircraft maintenance manual (AMM).

questions.question: If the flap drive motor assembly drives the flaps too much or too little, what is the likely cause?
questions.explanation: Excessive or insufficient flap travel is commonly traced to misadjusted or faulty limit switches controlling the drive motor.

questions.question: At the manufacturing plant, final assembly of the aircraft typically starts with what?
questions.explanation: Final assembly generally begins by bringing together the fuselage subassemblies before mating the wings, empennage, and other major components.

questions.question: Which cable size/type is typically used for trim tabs, engine controls, and indicator controls?
questions.explanation: Lighter-duty systems such as trim tabs, engine controls, and indicators commonly use flexible medium-size cable rather than heavy-duty extra-flexible cable.

questions.question: Which patented process uses copper sleeves and can be used up to the full rated strength of a cable looped around a thimble?
questions.explanation: The Nicopress process crimps a copper sleeve around a cable looped through a thimble, achieving the cable's full rated strength.

questions.question: What is the first step in removal of the landing gear?
options: B. Disconnect the wheel speed sensor
C. Remove the tire and wheel
questions.explanation: Before any landing gear component is disconnected, the hydraulic system must be depressurized to prevent injury or uncontrolled movement.

questions.question: Leveling and fixed-surface alignment checks should be performed in what kind of environment?
options: A. An enclosed area (protected from wind and sun)
C. Direct sunlight for best visibility
questions.explanation: Leveling and alignment work is done in an enclosed hangar area to avoid wind, temperature, and sunlight effects on the readings.

questions.question: What effect does wash-out have on a wing?
options: A. It increases lift at the tip
B. It has no effect on lift
C. It decreases lift (toward the tip)
questions.explanation: Because wash-out reduces the angle of incidence toward the tip, it reduces the lift generated by the outer wing sections.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rigging an aircraft?
options: A. To reduce the aircraft's empty weight
B. To ensure the structure has the proper flight characteristics
questions.explanation: Rigging aligns the airframe and flight controls so the aircraft exhibits its designed, proper flight characteristics.

questions.question: When rigging the aileron, a control lock is placed between the aileron and flap to hold the aileron in what position?
questions.explanation: The control lock holds the aileron in its neutral (streamlined) position while rigging measurements and adjustments are made.

questions.question: Where can specified torque values for fasteners be found?
options: A. On the fastener packaging only
B. In the pilot's operating handbook
C. In the aircraft maintenance manual
questions.explanation: Torque values for specific fasteners and applications are specified in the aircraft maintenance manual.

questions.question: The dihedral angle is formed by the intersection of the plane of the wing (or horizontal stabilizer) and what reference?
questions.explanation: Dihedral angle is measured between the wing (or stabilizer) plane and the aircraft's lateral axis (a horizontal reference line).

questions.question: When a control surface is mounted on a balance stand, a downward movement of the trailing edge below the horizontal position indicates what?
questions.explanation: If the trailing edge drops below horizontal on a balance stand, the surface is heavier aft of the hinge line, i.e., underbalanced.

questions.question: What is the first step in the assembly process of the landing gear?
options: A. Install the wheel and tire
questions.explanation: Before mounting the landing gear, the attachment/mounting area must be inspected to confirm it is airworthy and ready to accept the gear.

questions.question: What component is used in a cable system to adjust cable tension?
questions.explanation: Turnbuckles allow technicians to lengthen or shorten a cable assembly slightly, adjusting the tension to the specified value.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically a reason to perform a symmetry check?
options: B. Suspected damage from a hard landing
C. A reported control asymmetry or handling issue
questions.explanation: Routine component servicing alone does not normally trigger a symmetry check; symmetry checks are prompted by damage, repairs, or handling concerns.

questions.question: Which document provides the specific location description for placing a spirit level during leveling?
options: A. The Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS)
B. The weight and balance report
questions.explanation: The TCDS and associated structural repair/maintenance data specify where leveling points and spirit level locations are on the airframe.

questions.question: Which tool is used to check that the aircraft is level?
options: C. A plumb bob (with a spirit level or grid plate)
questions.explanation: A plumb bob, often combined with a spirit level or grid plate, is used to confirm the aircraft is longitudinally and laterally level.

questions.question: Where is pertinent rigging information for an aircraft typically found?
options: C. The Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) and maintenance manual
questions.explanation: Rigging data, leveling points, and control surface travel limits are found in the TCDS and the aircraft's maintenance manual.

questions.question: When the trailing edge moves up above the horizontal line when the surface is balanced at its hinge line, this indicates what?
questions.explanation: If the trailing edge rises above horizontal, the surface is nose-heavy relative to the hinge, which is called overbalance.

questions.question: The angle between the lateral axis and a line passing through the wing's center (wingtip to wingtip, as viewed from the front) defines what?
questions.explanation: Dihedral is the upward angle of the wings relative to the horizontal (lateral axis) reference line, viewed from the front of the aircraft.

questions.question: Which cable size is commonly used for trim tabs, engine controls, and indicator controls?
questions.explanation: 7x7 cable's medium flexibility makes it suitable for lighter-duty applications like trim tabs, engine controls, and indicator systems.

questions.question: A nut classified under medium fit falls under which class?
questions.explanation: Thread fit classifications run from loose (Class 1) to close (Class 4/5), with Class 3 commonly representing a medium fit.

questions.question: Fairleads should never deflect the alignment of a cable more than how many degrees from a straight line?
questions.explanation: Fairleads are intended for only slight cable deflection; standard practice limits this to no more than about 3 degrees from a straight line.

questions.question: What is the first procedure in the disassembly of a stabilizer?
questions.explanation: As with most structural disassembly tasks, the first step is to observe the applicable safety procedures before any components are disturbed.

questions.question: Which tool is used to measure the tightness of a bolt or nut?
questions.explanation: A torque wrench measures and applies a specified rotational force (torque) when tightening a bolt or nut.

questions.question: What tool is used to measure control surface deflection angles?
questions.explanation: The universal propeller protractor, despite its name, is commonly used to measure control surface deflection angles during rigging.

questions.question: What is the longitudinal difference in the position of the wings of a biplane called?
questions.explanation: Stagger describes the fore-and-aft offset between the upper and lower wings of a biplane.

questions.question: Before checking the position or angle of the main component of an aircraft, the aircraft must be what?
questions.explanation: Accurate rigging measurements require the aircraft to first be jacked and leveled to a known reference attitude.

questions.question: What do large aircraft incorporate in their control cable systems to automatically maintain a given cable tension?
questions.explanation: Tension regulators automatically compensate for temperature-induced expansion/contraction of the airframe, keeping cable tension within limits.

questions.question: What tool is used to measure cable tension?
questions.explanation: A tensiometer measures the tension in a control cable by reading the force needed to deflect the cable a set amount.

questions.question: How is a kinked or damaged (impacted) cable typically identified during inspection?
options: A. By measuring its electrical resistance
B. By rubbing a rag along the cable to catch on broken wire strands
C. By weighing a sample length
questions.explanation: Running a cloth or rag along a cable will snag on broken wires or burrs, helping technicians detect internal damage.

questions.question: What is the first step in rigging the elevator?
options: A. The trim tab is removed
B. The cable tension is adjusted
questions.explanation: Elevator rigging typically begins with measuring the existing control surface travel before making any adjustments.

questions.question: What should you inspect while rigging the flap system?
options: A. Only the flap paint condition
B. Only the cabin pressurization system
C. Whether the motor/drive assembly is moving the flaps too much or too little
questions.explanation: Flap rigging checks whether the drive motor and mechanism produce the correct amount of flap travel, neither too much nor too little.

questions.question: What is the difference between the angles of incidence of the upper and lower wings of a biplane called?
questions.explanation: Decalage refers to the difference in angle of incidence between the upper and lower wings of a biplane.

questions.question: The aircraft is leveled about which axes?
questions.explanation: Leveling an aircraft requires it to be level both laterally (wingtip to wingtip) and longitudinally (nose to tail).

questions.question: Which of the following describes a major part division used during aircraft manufacturing?
options: A. Left wing, right wing, and tail only
B. Engine, wing, and avionics bay only
C. Front section, mid-section, and aft section
questions.explanation: Large transport aircraft are commonly built and assembled in major fuselage sections such as front, mid, and aft sections.

questions.question: What is used to form the circular shape of a fuselage during manufacturing?
questions.explanation: Jigs (mating/forming jigs) hold frames and formers in their correct circular/contoured positions during fuselage assembly.

questions.question: A method of producing subassemblies of aircraft major parts and then assembling the major parts together is called what?
questions.explanation: Production body break describes building the aircraft in separate major subassemblies (sections) that are later joined together.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes aircraft rigging?
options: A. It's done whenever there is a fault in the alignment of the aircraft
B. It's done only once, at the factory
C. It's done only after an engine change
questions.explanation: Rigging is performed as needed, whenever misalignment of structure or controls is identified, not on a one-time or engine-specific basis.

questions.question: A nut classified under loose fit falls under which class?
questions.explanation: Class 1 fit represents the loosest of the standard thread fit classifications.

questions.question: A nut classified under close fit falls under which class?
questions.explanation: Class 4 fit represents a close (tighter) thread fit compared with the looser Class 1-3 fits.

questions.question: Lengthening the rear strut will move the wing toward what condition?
questions.explanation: Lengthening the rear strut lowers the trailing edge relative to the front attachment, introducing wash-out at that wing station.

questions.question: Which type of terminal fitting is suitable for use on civil aircraft cables up to and including the full rated cable strength?
questions.explanation: Swaged terminals are mechanically compressed onto the cable end and are approved for use up to the full rated strength of the cable.

questions.question: When checking a cable system, no more than how many threads should be exposed on either side of a turnbuckle barrel?
questions.explanation: Standard practice limits exposed turnbuckle threads to no more than 3 on either side, ensuring adequate thread engagement for safety.

questions.question: Which of the following comes last when rigging the rudder control system?
options: B. Locking the rudder in neutral
C. Connecting the cables to the rudder horn
questions.explanation: Cable tension is typically measured and fine-tuned as the final check after the rudder linkage has been connected and roughly set.

questions.question: Lengthening the rear strut will do what to the angle of incidence?
questions.explanation: Lengthening the rear strut rotates the wing's trailing edge down, which decreases the wing's angle of incidence.

questions.question: What term describes the effort to maintain balance when a control surface is subjected to movement on the aircraft in flight?
questions.explanation: Dynamic balance addresses how a control surface behaves and stays balanced while moving in flight, as opposed to static (at-rest) balance.

questions.question: The incidence angle is usually checked at how many specified positions on the wing to ensure it is free from twist?
questions.explanation: Checking the angle of incidence at a minimum of two spanwise positions lets technicians confirm the wing has no unintended twist between them.

questions.question: What is the first step while rigging the aileron?
options: C. Lock the control yoke/control surface in the neutral position
questions.explanation: Before measuring or adjusting aileron travel, the cockpit control and the surface itself are locked in the neutral position as a reference.

questions.question: What term describes the tendency of an object to remain stationary when supported from its own center of gravity?
questions.explanation: Static balance describes a control surface's tendency to stay put (not rotate) when supported exactly at its center of gravity.

questions.question: What is a check to determine that the wing and tail are symmetrical about the aircraft's longitudinal axis called?
questions.explanation: A symmetry check confirms that corresponding structures (wings, tail surfaces) are positioned identically on each side of the aircraft's centerline.
